sub_items.requirement: Requirements of 13.1.1 applied to oxygen concentrations up to 25% at one atmosphere or partial pressures up to 27.5 kPa for higher atmospheric pressures
No sources of ignition discovered in an OXYGEN RICH ENVIRONMENT in NORMAL and SINGLE FAULT CONDITIONS - condition 1: temperature of material raised to its ignition temperature

No sources of ignition - condition 2: temperatures affected solder or solder joints causing loosening, short circuiting, or other failures causing sparking or increasing material temperature to its ignition temperature
No sources of ignition - condition 3: parts affecting safety cracked or changed outer shape exposing temperatures higher than 300°C or sparks due to overheating
No sources of ignition - condition 4: temperatures of parts or components exceeded 300°C, atmosphere was 100% oxygen, contact material solder, and fuel cotton
Condition 5: sparks provided adequate energy for ignition by exceeding limits of Figs 35 to 37, atmosphere was 100% oxygen, contact material solder, and fuel cotton
Deviations from worst case limits in 4) and 5) based on lower oxygen concentrations or less flammable fuels justified and documented in RISK MANAGEMENT FILE
Alternative test did not identify existence of ignition sources at highest voltage or current
A safe upper limit determined by dividing upper limit of voltage or current with safety margin factor of three

semantic_fragments.content: For clause 11.1.2.2: APPLIED PARTS surface temperature must not exceed 41°C (or if it does, this must be disclosed in the instruction manual). Conditions for safe contact such as duration or condition of the PATIENT must be documented. Clinical effects with respect to characteristics such as body surface, maturity of PATIENTS, medications being taken, or surface pressure must be documented in the RISK MANAGEMENT FILE. Analysis documented in the RISK MANAGEMENT FILE must show that APPLIED PART temperatures are not affected by operation of ME EQUIPMENT including SINGLE FAULT CONDITIONS.

For clause 11.2.2.1 regarding fire prevention in OXYGEN RICH ENVIRONMENTS: Requirements of 13.1.1 apply to oxygen concentrations up to 25% at one atmosphere or partial pressures up to 27.5 kPa for higher atmospheric pressures. The device under test is not used in conjunction with oxygen rich environments, hence all sub-clauses are N/A. Safe upper limits are determined by dividing upper limit of voltage or current with a safety margin factor of three.
